scope: Final visible draft, deployed JSON and rendered link parity, exact article/action blobs, correction-train chronology, held-action state, source-byte versus token claims, command and owner-gate surfaces, and current review discovery. Read-only review; no article acceptance, action admission, workflow, runtime, merge, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The simultaneous three-train stall is invented
findings.location: Line 11: PR #456 and PR #462 allegedly stalled all three trains simultaneously.
findings.explanation: PR #456 records an October 22 action-decision boundary. October 22 acceptance merged at 02:19 UTC and October 23 acceptance merged at 05:36 UTC, while the diagnostic display repair #462 did not merge until 06:22 UTC and changed no article or queue data. The primary chronology cannot support one simultaneous blocker across all three trains.
findings.correction: Report #456 as an October 22 action-decision repair and #462 as an October 23 current-request display repair. Preserve their separate chronology and remove the three-train causal claim.

findings.title: October 24 retained three Needs review suggestions
findings.location: Lines 46 and 73: no held-action step fired because October 24 suggestions were not in Needs review.
findings.explanation: The native acceptance receipt records actionReview pending, evidence-required, and three held candidate IDs. The accepted-source review repeats that exactly three suggestions remain Needs review and non-dispatchable.
findings.correction: State that October 24 completed article-only acceptance with three held suggestions. No separate held-action run occurred; do not infer an empty held set.

findings.title: Helpdesk check-ins are linked as nonexistent GitHub pull requests
findings.location: Lines 64 and 97: check-ins #52 and #53 link to workstation-yuri pull requests 52 and 53.
findings.explanation: Workstation-yuri PR #3 describes #52 and #53 as Helpdesk/Mini check-ins. The rendered /pull/52 and /pull/53 targets do not resolve to GitHub records, so the article manufactures repository pull-request identities for non-PR observations.
findings.correction: Identify #52 and #53 as Helpdesk check-in identities. Link an actual durable check-in receipt if public; otherwise attribute the observation to PR #3 without manufacturing GitHub PR links or merge controls.

findings.title: A source-byte hold is turned into a token-limit prediction
findings.location: Lines 107 and 123: 250,399 bytes against a 131,072-byte source limit becomes a claim that the token limit will be hit in production.
findings.explanation: Issue #386 explicitly says byte limits do not prove token-window fit. The October 23 receipt records the 250,399-byte source hold before model contact and says token and verifier fit were not tested.
findings.correction: Describe a per-source byte-limit hold before model entry. Keep tokenizer, model-window, output-reserve, and future-case fit unknown.

findings.title: Suggested-action commands are not executable interfaces
findings.location: Line 119: /review-draft merge, /ground-facts, and /audit-hooks are presented as commands.
findings.explanation: The pinned workflow index exposes no such command surfaces. Later source-bound custody explicitly calls the original payloads unsupported commands retained for audit, not executable recommendations.
findings.correction: Preserve candidate IDs and payload text as held historical evidence, label the commands unsupported and non-dispatchable, and name the real supervised PR-review or owner-decision route.

findings.title: The action card invents cross-date and sole-blocker prerequisites
findings.location: Lines 103 and 119-121: PR #452 cannot advance until #450 merges, and a manual ground-facts check is the only blocker for core #572.
findings.explanation: PRs #450 and #452 are independent source-pinned review publications; neither establishes a cross-date readiness dependency. Core #572 already records fact/provenance contract checks, a separate independent review, bounded pilot limits, and a broader canonical-review-before-adoption gate.
findings.correction: Treat #450 and #452 as independently supervised records; ordering is an operator preference unless separately decided. Describe #572 as draft pending canonical review/adoption with bounded pilot limits, not a nonexistent command or sole manual fact check.

findings.title: Action review is incorrectly presented as a prerequisite for article acceptance
findings.location: The Suggested actions card says acceptance remains blocked until action review completes.
findings.explanation: October 23 acceptance #460 and October 24 acceptance #464 demonstrate article-only acceptance with suggestions held for independent review.
findings.correction: Say article acceptance may proceed with uncertain actions visibly Needs review; action admission and closure remain blocked until verified.

findings.title: The Helpdesk replay observation lacks an independently accessible receipt
findings.location: Lines 64 and 97: check-in #53 replay is called confirmation that the Helpdesk service is live and functional.
findings.explanation: Workstation-yuri PR #3 reports the observation, but the article's #52/#53 links are nonexistent GitHub pull requests and no independently accessible check-in receipt is linked from the article.
findings.correction: Attribute the runtime statement to PR #3 and label independent replay verification unavailable, or link a durable check-in record binding observation time, service revision, and replay result.

findings.title: Morning Cockpit #60's merge-readiness claim lacks an owner disposition
findings.location: Lines 109 and 124: PR #60 has passed review and has no documented blocker.
findings.explanation: PR #60 contains generated cleanup and validation statements but no evidenced owner merge disposition. Related issue #57 concerns PR #56's source-record contract and does not establish a hard merge prerequisite for #60. The #386 receipt requires both surfaces in the evidence census, not a direct dependency. These records do not prove a blocker exists for #60.
findings.correction: Report #60 as open without an evidenced owner merge disposition. Identify #57 as a separate related contract concern. Infer neither merge readiness nor a hard #57 gate for #60.
